checks.claim: The title, setup and live world render without page overflow.
checks.evidence: Title and setup were observed at 1280x720; body scroll bounds matched the viewport after the title-art overflow fix.

checks.claim: Human and Toon starts are playable in a live 3D world.
checks.evidence: Human/Panzer and Toon/Gear Shepherd starts rendered with fixed elevated camera, villages and safe starting cores; a latched W tap moved Player 1.

checks.claim: Local Player 2 input is independent.
checks.evidence: In Toon co-op, an ArrowRight tap changed only Player 2's recorded X coordinate from 67.000 to 67.901.

checks.claim: Save restoration preserves position and world outcome.
checks.evidence: Autosave plus reload restored Player 1's exact recorded X/Z coordinates; a clean later reload restored THE GAME IS WON - WORLD CONTINUES.

checks.claim: The 24-hour finale is winnable by robots and play continues.
checks.evidence: The localhost-only finale route opened the specialist-brain flow, deployed village robots, resolved the boss through robot damage, persisted the win and returned to the live world.

checks.claim: The clean final runtime has no new browser console warnings or errors.
checks.evidence: A new tab loaded the saved won world with two canvases and an empty warn/error log query.

checks.claim: Wobble Pond remembers released species and turns that memory into visible ecology and useful play.
checks.evidence: A Gossip Carp release created its permanent 3D pond monument, changed the region HUD to POND: 1/3 SPECIES, restricted pond fishing to the established species and enabled one ecology basket per saved world day. A second claim on day 26 was visibly refused.

checks.claim: Cooking recipes create explicit, long-term world consequences instead of generic stat food.
checks.evidence: The live cook-off displayed all four world effects. Completing Sunberry Upside-Down Pie activated PET WHISPER for 60 saved-world minutes and exposed that effect in the normal HUD. Automated coverage also proves quest previews, robot overclocking and hybrid-drop unlock gating.

checks.claim: Pet Whisper reveals a miniature robot's actual terms without bypassing the rare-stone bond economy.
checks.evidence: With zero stones, Sprig-0's live modal named Sunberry Upside-Down Pie and its gardener ability, warned that bonding still needs a stone, and kept STONE STILL REQUIRED disabled.

checks.claim: Fishing, cooking and robot-conversation interactions do not punish the player for reading or participating.
checks.evidence: An initial pond observation exposed nearby enemy damage during the activity. The local sanctuary rule was added and retested at the pond, cook-off and Sprig-0; health remained 100 after five-second observation windows and the final browser log was empty.

checks.claim: Equipment branches are understandable and manipulable in the live inventory instead of being decorative text.
checks.evidence: At 1280x720, the staged Human Springpan card visibly separated ACTIVE MECHANIC from LIVE DRAWBACK, showed the equipped branch in the paper doll and offered the other named branch for 0 bolts. No card text clipped or overlapped.

checks.claim: Human Second Opinion is free once, while repeated branch manipulation has an escalating saved cost.
checks.evidence: One bounded retune changed BONK radius +25% to Every 5th attack launches breakfast without changing the 20-bolt balance; the next offer was 11 bolts. A second retune reduced the visible balance to 9 and raised the following offer to 14 bolts.

checks.claim: A retuned equipment branch changes visible live-world combat behavior.
checks.evidence: After retuning Springpan and closing the inventory, five bounded attacks produced a visible BREAKFAST! world-space combat word. The inventory remained closed, health remained 100, the won world continued and the browser log stayed empty.

checks.claim: Bonded miniature robots are selectable field partners with legible roles, integrity and distinct specialties.
checks.evidence: The live Miniature Robot Workshop displayed all six robots, their locations, jobs, requirements, integrity and different ability descriptions. Selecting Siren Sue changed the HUD and active workshop summary to 64/64 Town Crier, and the robot was visibly present beside the hero. The initially malformed close glyph was corrected to a real multiplication sign and retested.

checks.claim: A miniature specialty commands neutral robots without silently converting bonded partners.
checks.evidence: Using Siren Sue's live Civic Siren action produced its command result, applied a saved-world cooldown and left bonded robots excluded from the neutral command pool.

checks.claim: A Golden Duck catch actually rebuilds a downed bonded miniature.
checks.evidence: Moss Boss began visibly down at 0/68 with Ranger Audit disabled and Golden Duck required. Completing the staged live fishing interaction produced GOLDEN DUCK!, named Moss Boss in the result, restored it to 68/68, re-enabled Ranger Audit and updated the workshop to ACTIVE FIELD PARTNER. The final browser log was empty.

checks.claim: A story decision explains both permanent outcomes before the player commits.
checks.evidence: At 1280x720, The River Is on Strike displayed two unclipped branches. Each card separately named its narrative preview and WORLD CHANGE: either 45% faster river movement or one additional fish per ordinary catch.

checks.claim: A completed side adventure creates a persistent, revisitable change in the rendered world rather than only a saved label.
checks.evidence: Choosing BUILD THE ROBOT FERRY LANE completed the adventure, constructed a bright miniature ferry procession in the Sizzlebank river, added a REVIEW action, showed MEMORY: FERRY LANE in the region HUD, created a world-map memory marker and changed the journal card to WORLD REMEMBERS with the exact movement mechanic. Interacting with the set-piece recited its saved-world memory and consequence.

checks.claim: The selected story outcome survives an ordinary reload and remains safe to read.
checks.evidence: Navigating from the localhost-only story route to the ordinary game route and continuing the save rebuilt the same ferry set-piece, HUD memory and REVIEW interaction without reopening the choice. The first observation exposed one enemy hit immediately after the decision; memory sites were added to the activity sanctuary and the exact path was retested for more than five seconds at 100 health. Final browser logs were empty.

checks.claim: The 23rd-hour event enters gradually instead of appearing as one abrupt finale toast.
checks.evidence: Repeated 1280x720 screenshots used the same central-meadow camera at 23:04, 23:31 and 23:52 saved play. The HUD reported omen stages 1, 3 and 4 at 8%, 52% and 88%; a subtle gray-violet needle grew into opaque structures while the daylight, fog and ground palette shifted visibly between samples.

checks.claim: Losing persists as a damaged but playable saved world.
checks.evidence: Ruin stage 3 rendered a purple rally beacon, rubble and world wounds at 62% overrun. Navigating to the ordinary non-QA route and continuing the save retained ruin at 63%, kept the rally interaction and preserved Sprig-0's resistance damage at 48/58. The original village battle team was not recreated.

checks.claim: Post-loss recovery uses only the player's living bonded miniatures and their saved integrity.
checks.evidence: The rally prompt counted 5/5 living bonded robots. Starting resistance spawned five distinct miniature actors around the visitor, changed the HUD to state that player attacks deal zero direct damage, exposed visitor integrity and robot survivors, and disabled rally re-entry while combat was active. An abandoned attempt's pet damage survived an ordinary reload.

checks.claim: Bonded robots can win the desperate recovery and return to a playable scarred world.
checks.evidence: The staged resistance visibly progressed from 95% to 56%, then 5% visitor integrity with five robots still answering. It resolved to Patchwork Vale survives, recorded three resistance attempts, and KEEP LIVING IN THE WON WORLD returned to THE GAME IS WON · WORLD CONTINUES while the ruin structures remained visible.

checks.claim: Ordinary enemy species create distinct, readable comedy problems instead of sharing one contact-only behavior.
checks.evidence: At 1280x720, repeated samples on the bounded combat route visibly showed Hecklecrab's open-mic heckle text, a flying paperwork form with a tell ring, a purple Moodcloud puddle at the hero, and a Tax Goose stealing bolts before fleeing. Source and automated contracts separately cover the Loose Screw dash. The hero was staged without a companion so these observations were not produced by automatic pet attacks.

checks.claim: Winning an ordinary fight leaves a memorable species-specific joke and recoverable theft.
checks.evidence: The Moodcloud defeat produced a visible rainbow aftermath. In a separate bounded restitution route, the HUD began at 2 bolts with 2 stored on the Tax Goose; defeating it changed the visible HUD to 4, displayed GOOSE REFUND PROCESSED, and left the world-space line REFUND WITH FEATHERS!.

checks.claim: Settlements contain mixed residents with understandable routines and saved useful favors.
checks.evidence: Kettlewick visibly contained Human, Toon and miniature-robot residents at the same time. Auntie Whistle exposed HELP AUNTIE WHISTLE · ROUTINE · RUNAWAY SIGN STRAIGHTENER; completing it paid one Sunberry, changed the action to CHECK ON, and an ordinary non-QA reload retained CHECK ON without replaying the completion reward. A later separated sample showed citizens at different route positions.

checks.claim: Village night is visually and behaviorally different from village day.
checks.evidence: The deterministic 22:00 Kettlewick sample was visibly dimmer than day, showed bright street-lamp bulbs, placed residents at their home positions, and exposed Auntie Whistle's OFF DUTY · PRETENDING TO SLEEP status. This is a separated state comparison; no sub-frame animation timing is claimed.

checks.claim: Cooking is a readable three-round skill contest rather than three identical timing taps.
checks.evidence: At 1280x720, the Sizzlebank menu named Mayor Marmalade, exposed SCORE TO BEAT 48 and stated that the ladder contains finite permanent lessons. Separated live states showed CHOP, STIR and PLATE with different instructions, track treatments, target positions and running player/rival scores. Chop visibly recorded 53, Stir recorded 82, and the completed three-round run resolved to a visible 53–48 victory. These are separated observations; no sub-frame input or animation cadence is claimed.

checks.claim: A cook-off result creates a useful world meal and finite persistent rival progress without requiring repeated level grinding.
checks.evidence: The 53–48 victory activated PET WHISPER for 45 world minutes and awarded Civic Knife Permit · CHOP zone permanently 8% wider. After navigating to the ordinary non-QA route and continuing the saved world, the region HUD retained Pet Whisper, the cook-off advanced to The Wok Goblin, and the menu retained both the permanent lesson and Personal best: 53. Automated system evidence separately proves that losing still creates the selected quality-scaled world meal and cannot erase or duplicate an earned first-win lesson.

checks.claim: The Human hero uses a real licensed skeletal asset with relocatable provenance in the live game.
checks.evidence: At 1280x720, the focused production route visibly rendered the Quaternius Human and directly reported production, human-casual-a, CC0-1.0, 31 bones and the idle clip. The exact packaged GLB hash is enforced separately by deterministic evidence.

checks.claim: Locomotion and attack use authored clips without replacing the class-specific comedy weapon language.
checks.evidence: A bounded W input directly reported walk. Pan Slap directly reported slash plus attack:slash while the live Human changed to the authored strike and retained the oversized pan/cue language; a separated later state reported idle. No sub-frame cadence is inferred from these observations.

checks.claim: Reduced-motion mode keeps the production skeleton static while preserving readable action feedback.
checks.evidence: The visible Reduced motion control was enabled, Pan Slap reported reduced-static, and the gold action cue remained visible around the unchanged production stance. The option was restored afterward.

checks.claim: Production-asset failure leaves a visible playable original Human rather than a loading gate.
checks.evidence: The deterministic forced-fallback route reported fallback, procedural, original-code and qa-forced-safe-fallback; the original Human remained visible, accepted Pan Slap, made no failed asset request and produced no browser warning or error.

observation_method.cadence: Repeated semantic samples and screenshots; no rolling-buffer capability was exposed, so sub-frame animation timing was not claimed.
